snippet.title: 6 Things in Your Garage That Matter More Than Any Survival Kit
snippet.description:
You don't need an expensive survival kit to be more prepared for the next disaster.

You may already have some of the most useful emergency tools sitting in your garage right now — and you probably walk past them every day.

In this video, we're breaking down 6 ordinary things in your garage that can become extremely valuable during a long power outage, storm, grid failure, or emergency.

You'll discover:

• Stored water — the resource everything else depends on
• Your water heater — a large tank that may contain 30–50 gallons of water
• An adjustable wrench — a simple tool that can help you shut off your home's gas and water mains
• Your car — a potential charger, radio, climate-controlled space, and source of small amounts of power when used safely
• Stored fuel — gasoline, propane, or charcoal that can provide options when normal utilities fail
• Your bicycle — transportation that doesn't depend on fuel, batteries, or functioning roads

The biggest lesson is simple:

Survival isn't always about buying more gear. It's about understanding what you already own.

The video also covers important safety precautions, including why you should never run a vehicle inside a closed garage because of carbon monoxide, and why gasoline, propane, charcoal, and cooking equipment must be handled and stored properly.

And when roads are blocked, flooded, or gas stations can't pump fuel, that old bicycle in your garage may suddenly become one of your most useful assets.

You may already be more prepared than you think.

Before you spend money on another survival kit, look around your garage.

snippet.description:
When an earthquake strikes, knowing what to do in the first few seconds can help protect you from injury.

This short earthquake safety video demonstrates the essential DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON procedure:

DROP to your hands and knees before the shaking knocks you down.
COVER your head and neck under a sturdy desk or table.
HOLD ON and stay protected until the shaking stops.
Stay away from windows, glass, shelves, and falling objects.
Do not run outside while dangerous debris may be falling.
After the shaking stops, stay alert for aftershocks and check your surroundings for hazards.

Remember: DROP • COVER • HOLD ON

snippet.description:

最近、自然災害が増えていて
「いざという時、自分に何ができるんだろう？」
と不安になることもありますよね🥺

今回は、特別な防災グッズがなくても
家にあるものですぐ試せる防災ハック3選をまとめました💡

① ペットボトルで簡易ランタン
懐中電灯＋水入りペットボトルで、周りをやさしく照らせます✨

② ペットボトルで簡易水道
小さな穴を開けて、断水時の手洗いや水の使用量を減らす工夫に◎

③ 断水時のトイレ対策
断水中に誤って流さないための準備や、袋・新聞紙などを使った簡易的な対策を紹介しています🚽

災害はいつ起こるかわからないからこそ、
「知っている」だけでも備えになります。

地震や台風など、もしもの時に思い出せるように
【保存】しておいてね🌿

家族や大切な人にも【シェア】して
一緒に防災について考えてみてください☺️

忙しいママでも無理なくできる
暮らしの工夫や、ゆる掃除・ライフハックを発信中🫧
フォローして他の投稿もチェックしてね♡

⚠️火や電気、水を使う方法は、周囲の安全を確認して十分注意して行ってください。

United Way of Southeast Louisiana and our friends at the National Weather Service have tips and resources to help you organize your finances and prepare for severe weather and disaster. 

United Way plays a vital role in helping communities prepare for disaster. Through a partnership with Verizon, this work has expanded further to include developing disaster preparedness workshops for community residents and non-profits. 

Learn more at UnitedWaySELA.org/Disaster.
